findings.evidence: Lines 90–94 select every associated author's comments, and lines 108–145 consume both marker types from that shared list; COORDINATION.md’s review-state contract requires comments by the canonical reviewer.
findings.fix: Validate the exact canonical reviewer/App identity for both signal types, rather than filtering only by `author_association`.
findings.issue: Both scoreboard verdicts and in-progress markers are trusted from any OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR, so any collaborator can forge `ready-to-merge` or `review-in-progress`; repo association does not identify the canonical reviewer.

findings.evidence: Lines 185–189 query only `--label review-in-progress`; all other reconciliation triggers require a future PR/build/comment event, while README.md relegates existing PR coverage to a local backfill command.
findings.fix: Add an automated initial/full reconciliation of all open PRs, or make the scheduled sweep reconcile all open PRs.
findings.issue: The scheduled sweep only lists PRs already carrying `review-in-progress`, so existing open PRs without a status label never receive one unless an undocumented deployment-time backfill is manually run; this violates “every open PR exactly one status label.”

summary: The derivation can accept forged review signals, and deployment does not establish the claimed label invariant for existing open PRs.
